gr-em-1.text: Now it is time to return. Take a deeper breath in, and feel energy coming back into your body.

gr-em-2.text: Stretch your fingers and your toes. Let your breathing become brighter and fuller.

gr-em-3.text: And when you are ready, open your eyes. Feeling awake, alert, and quietly glad. If you like, write down one thing you noticed before you carry on with your day.

gr-ind-1.text: Let your eyes close, and take a slow breath in. And let it go, a little longer on the way out.

gr-ind-2.text: Again, breathe in gently. And breathe out, letting your shoulders soften and your hands rest.

gr-ind-3.text: Let your breathing find its own rhythm now. Feel the weight of your body, supported. With each breath out, your mind becomes a little quieter, a little more spacious.

gr-int-1.text: Being grateful does not mean pretending that everything is fine. It simply means that, alongside whatever is hard, you can also see what is good. Both can be true.

gr-int-2.text: Over the coming days, you may find that you notice small good things a little more easily. A taste. A kindness. A moment of ease. And each time, you can pause, for one breath, and take it in.

gr-one-1.text: Now, let your mind drift back over today, or yesterday. See if you can find one small good thing. It might be a warm drink. A moment of sunlight. A kind word. Something that went a little better than expected. Take your time. I will be quiet for a few moments while you look.

gr-one-2.text: Whatever you have found, bring it closer. Where were you? What could you see, or hear, or taste? Let the moment become vivid again, as if it is happening now.

gr-one-3.text: Notice how it feels in your body to remember this. Perhaps a little warmth, or a softening somewhere. Let yourself enjoy it for a few more breaths.

gr-pre-1.text: Welcome. For the next few minutes, we are going to slow down and notice a few good things. They do not have to be big. And if nothing comes to mind at some point, that is completely fine. Just rest, and listen.

gr-three-1.text: And now, think of one thing in your life that you rely on. Something so familiar that you rarely notice it. A place to sleep. A friend. Your eyesight. Clean water from a tap.

gr-three-2.text: For just a moment, imagine your life without it. Notice what would be missing.

gr-three-3.text: And now, come back. It is here. You have it. Let that land, as a quiet sense of good fortune.

gr-two-1.text: Now, bring to mind a person who has helped you, or cared about you. It could be someone from long ago, or someone you saw this week. Let their face appear in your mind.

gr-two-2.text: Remember something they did for you. It may have cost them time, or effort, or thought. They did not have to do it. And they did.

gr-two-3.text: Silently, in your own words, thank them. Imagine that they can hear you, and notice how they might look as they receive it. I will give you a quiet moment for this.

ic-b1-1.text: You can let your eyes close. Let the breath flow in and out without any force. I will be quiet now, and let you breathe.

ic-b1-2.text: You are doing well. If your mind has wandered, simply come back to the sound of the wind. Soft belly. Relaxed shoulders.

ic-b2-1.text: A few more quiet breaths now. In with the rising wind. Out as it settles.

ic-em-1.text: Now take a fuller breath in, and stretch gently. Feel your feet on the floor.

ic-em-2.text: Open your eyes, and look around the room. You are awake, alert, and steady. Ready for whatever comes next.

ic-heart-1.text: As you keep breathing, bring your attention to the center of your chest. Imagine the breath flowing in and out through this place, around your heart.

ic-heart-2.text: Now, if you like, think of someone or something you appreciate. A person, a pet, a place you love. You do not need to think about it very hard. Just let the feeling of appreciation be here, as you breathe.

ic-heart-3.text: Keep breathing through the center of your chest. Steady, and smooth. Let that feeling of care settle in.

ic-pre-1.text: Welcome. This is a breathing practice for steadying your body and mind. Sit comfortably, with your back upright but relaxed, and let your hands rest.

ic-pre-2.text: In a moment you will hear the wind moving through the trees. As the wind rises, breathe in through your nose. As it settles, breathe out, slowly. The breath out is a little longer than the breath in.

ic-pre-3.text: Breathe gently. These are slow breaths, not big ones. If you ever feel light headed, simply return to your normal breathing, and join in again when you are ready.

ic-ret-1.text: The wind is quieting now. Let your breathing return to its natural rhythm. Notice how you feel. Perhaps a little steadier. A little clearer.

ic-ret-2.text: You can come back to this steady rhythm any time today, with just a few slow breaths.

ic-warm-1.text: Let us begin. Follow the wind. In as it rises. And out as it settles.

ic-warm-2.text: Good. Now the wind will slow down a little. Stay with it, smooth and easy.

lc-all-1.text: And now, let the light spread wider. To the people in your building, and on your street. To everyone in your town. Out across the country, and around the whole world. People waking up, people falling asleep. All of them, just like you, wishing to be happy.

lc-all-2.text: May all beings be safe. May all beings be happy.

lc-all-3.text: May all beings be healthy. May all beings live with ease.

lc-deep-1.text: Now bring your attention to the center of your chest. Imagine a small, warm light glowing there, like a candle, or the first sun of the morning.

lc-deep-2.text: With every breath in, the light grows a little brighter. With every breath out, its warmth spreads a little further. Through your chest. Into your shoulders. Down your arms. Gentle, and steady.

lc-em-1.text: Now it is time to return. Let the light settle back into the center of your chest, where it stays with you.

lc-em-2.text: Take a deeper breath in. Feel energy returning to your arms and legs. Stretch your fingers and your toes.

lc-em-3.text: And open your eyes. Awake, alert, and clear, carrying this warmth with you into the rest of your day.

lc-ind-1.text: Let your eyes close, and take a slow breath in. And let it go, a little longer on the way out.

lc-ind-2.text: Once more, breathe in gently. And breathe out, letting your face soften, and your shoulders drop.

lc-ind-3.text: Let your breathing settle into its own rhythm. Feel your body resting, supported, with nothing to do.

lc-loved-1.text: Now, bring to mind someone it is easy to care about. A good friend. A child. A grandparent. A pet. Someone who makes you smile when you think of them. Let them appear in front of you.

lc-loved-2.text: See their face. Feel how naturally you wish them well. And silently, offer them these words.

lc-loved-7.text: Imagine the warm light from your chest reaching them, and see them receive it. Rest in that feeling for a moment.

lc-neutral-1.text: Now, think of someone you hardly know. Someone you passed in the street, or who served you in a shop. You do not know their story. But just like you, they want to be happy, and they have their own worries.

lc-neutral-2.text: Picture them, and offer them the same wishes. May you be safe. May you be happy.

lc-neutral-3.text: May you be healthy. May you live with ease.

lc-pre-1.text: Welcome to this practice. Today we will offer kindness, first to someone you care about, then to yourself, and then outward to others. Whatever you feel, or do not feel, is fine. Your intention is enough.

lc-pre-2.text: If strong feelings come up at any time, you can always open your eyes, feel your feet on the floor, and simply rest with your breath.

lc-rest-1.text: Rest for a moment in this wide, warm feeling. You are part of it. The kindness you send out includes you too.

lc-rest-2.text: In the days ahead, you may notice moments of warmth toward the people around you, and toward yourself. A kind thought arriving on its own. Each time, the feeling grows a little more familiar.

lc-self-1.text: Now, turn that same kindness toward yourself. If that feels difficult, you might picture yourself as a young child. Or simply rest, and let the words wash over you.

lc-self-2.text: Like everyone, you have had hard days. Like everyone, you are doing the best you can. And like everyone, you deserve kindness.

lc-self-7.text: Let the warmth fill your whole body, from your head to your feet. There is nothing you have to earn. Just rest here.

qs-free-deep-1.text: In a moment, I will count down from ten to one. With each number, you can let yourself drift a little deeper into this calm, focused state, as though walking down a gentle staircase, one easy step at a time.

qs-free-deep-2.text: Ten. Stepping down. Nine. Deeper and more comfortable. Eight. Letting go of the day. Seven. Drifting down. Six. Calm and safe.

qs-free-deep-3.text: Five, halfway down, twice as relaxed. Four. Three. So peaceful now. Two. Almost there. And one. Deeply relaxed, and wonderfully focused.

qs-free-ego-1.text: Every hour that you breathe free, your confidence grows. Each urge that you ride out makes the next one weaker, and makes you stronger. You are learning that you can trust yourself.

qs-free-ego-2.text: And if you ever slip, you treat it as information, not as failure. You simply return to your plan, with kindness, and you carry on. Nothing can take away the progress you have made.

qs-free-ego-3.text: These ideas are yours now. They will keep working quietly in the back of your mind, long after this session ends, growing stronger each time you listen.

qs-free-em-1.text: In a moment, I will count from one up to five. With each number, energy and alertness will return, and at five your eyes will open, and you will feel refreshed and clear.

qs-free-em-2.text: One. Beginning to return. Two. Feeling energy flow back into your arms and legs. Three. Taking a deeper breath, and becoming aware of the room around you.

qs-free-em-3.text: Four. Your eyes are getting ready to open, your mind is bright and clear. And five. Eyes open. Wide awake, fully alert, and feeling good. Welcome back.

qs-free-ind-1.text: Begin by taking a slow breath in through your nose. And let it go, gently, through your mouth, a little longer on the way out.

qs-free-ind-2.text: Again, breathe in, slowly and comfortably. And release, letting your shoulders drop as the air leaves.

qs-free-ind-3.text: One more time. Breathe in clean, fresh air. And as you breathe out, allow your eyes to close, if they have not closed already.

qs-free-ind-4.text: Now let your breathing find its own easy rhythm. Notice the feeling of relaxation beginning at the top of your head, smoothing your forehead, softening the small muscles around your eyes, and loosening your jaw.

qs-free-ind-5.text: That comfort flows down through your neck and shoulders, down your arms, all the way to your fingertips. Your hands may begin to feel warm, or heavy, or pleasantly light. Whatever you notice is exactly right.

qs-free-ind-6.text: Let the relaxation move through your chest, where your breath is easy and unhurried. Down through your stomach, your hips, your legs, all the way to the soles of your feet. Now your whole body is resting.

qs-free-pre-1.text: Welcome. This session is here to support you as you become free from smoking. It works best alongside your quit plan, whether that includes nicotine replacement, medication, or the support of a doctor or a quit line.

qs-free-pre-2.text: Make sure you are somewhere safe and comfortable, where you can close your eyes for a while. There is nothing you have to get right. Simply listen, and let the words do the work.

qs-free-reh-1.text: Now imagine a morning in the days ahead. You wake, and you pour your coffee or your tea. In the past, this was a moment for a cigarette. But see yourself now, holding the warm cup, breathing deeply, and enjoying the taste more than you ever have. Calm, and free.

qs-free-reh-2.text: See yourself after a meal. You stand, you stretch, you take a few slow breaths, or a short walk. The old habit drifts by like a cloud, and you let it pass. You feel light, and quietly proud.

qs-free-reh-3.text: Imagine a stressful moment. Something goes wrong, and tension rises. And you notice that you press your thumb and finger together, you breathe out slowly, and the tension loosens. You handle it clearly, with a steady mind. You always could.

qs-free-reh-4.text: And picture yourself with friends, where others may be smoking. You are relaxed and comfortable. If someone offers, you smile and say, no thanks, I am good. And it feels true, because it is.

qs-free-sug-1.text: In this calm place, your mind is clear, and open to ideas that are good for you. So let these ideas settle in, as easily as breathing.

qs-free-sug-2.text: Your body is precious. It has carried you through every single day of your life. It breathes for you while you sleep. It heals you when you are hurt. And it has been waiting, patiently, for this moment.

qs-free-sug-3.text: You need your body to live. And so you choose to protect it, the way you would protect anyone you love. This is not about giving something up. This is about giving something back, to yourself.

qs-free-sug-4.text: Already, something in you is changing. You are becoming a person who breathes freely. A person whose lungs are clearing, whose heart is growing stronger, whose senses of taste and smell are waking up again. This is simply who you are now.

qs-free-sug-5.text: From time to time, an urge may still arrive. That is natural, and it is nothing to fear. An urge is only a wave. It rises, it reaches a peak, and then, every single time, it passes. Whether or not you smoke, the wave passes.

qs-free-sug-6.text: So when a wave comes, you do not need to fight it, and you do not need to obey it. You can simply notice it. You can say to yourself, there is an urge. And you can watch it rise, and crest, and fade away, while you stay steady, like someone watching the ocean from the shore.

qs-free-sug-7.text: Now, gently press the thumb and first finger of one hand together. This is your anchor. As you hold it, take one slow breath, and feel the calm you feel right now gather in that small point of touch.

qs-free-sug-8.text: Whenever you press your thumb and finger together, and take three slow breaths, this same calm returns to you. It becomes stronger every time you use it. You can relax your hand now, knowing your anchor is always with you.

qs-r10-1.text: Welcome. For the next ten minutes, we are going to move your attention slowly through your body. There is nothing to achieve. If a craving is here, it can stay in the background while we do this.

qs-r10-10.text: Move up into your chest. Notice your ribs widening and settling. Notice your heartbeat, if you can feel it. Your lungs are doing their work, and already they are beginning to clear.

qs-r10-11.text: Bring your attention to your upper back and your shoulders. So much tension gathers here. Simply notice it, and if your shoulders want to drop a little, let them.

qs-r10-12.text: Now let your attention travel down both arms. Upper arms, elbows, forearms, wrists.

qs-r10-13.text: And into your hands. Notice your palms, and each finger. These hands are free right now. Feel the air on your skin, or the surface they are resting on.

qs-r10-14.text: Move your attention to your neck and your throat. Notice the cool air passing in, and the warm air passing out.

qs-r10-15.text: Now your jaw. Your lips. Your tongue resting in your mouth. Your cheeks, your eyes, your forehead. Let your whole face be soft.

qs-r10-16.text: And now widen your attention to take in your whole body at once, from your feet to the top of your head. One whole body, breathing.

qs-r10-17.text: If the craving is still here, notice where it sits in this wider picture. It is one small sensation among many. You can carry it without acting on it, and it is already fading.

qs-r10-18.text: Take a deeper breath in, and feel energy returning. Stretch your fingers and your toes.

qs-r10-19.text: Breathe out, open your eyes fully, and look around you. You are alert, steady, and clear. Before you go back to your day, do one small thing for yourself: some water, a short walk, or a word with someone you trust. Well done.

qs-r10-2.text: Sit or stand comfortably. You can keep your eyes open, with a soft gaze, or let them close if you are somewhere safe.

qs-r10-3.text: Take a slow breath in. And let it go, a little longer on the way out.

qs-r10-4.text: Bring your attention all the way down to your feet. Notice your toes, the soles of your feet, your heels. Notice where they touch the floor or your shoes. Warm or cool, heavy or light. Simply notice.

qs-r10-5.text: Move your attention up into your ankles, your calves, and your shins. You are not trying to relax them. You are only noticing what is there.

qs-r10-6.text: Now your knees, and the large muscles of your thighs. Feel the weight of your legs, supported.

qs-r10-7.text: If your mind wanders to smoking, that is perfectly normal. Notice the thought, let it be, and gently bring your attention back to your body.

qs-r10-8.text: Bring your attention to your hips and your lower back. Notice any contact with the chair, any pressure, any ease.

qs-r10-9.text: Now your stomach. Feel it rise as you breathe in, and fall as you breathe out. There is no need to control the breath. Just watch it move.

qs-r2-1.text: You chose this instead of smoking. That is already a win. Stay with me for two minutes.

qs-r2-10.text: And release. Let your hands go soft.

qs-r2-11.text: The wave is passing. You chose to breathe free, and you just did. Now do one small thing: drink some water, or walk for a minute. Well done.

qs-r2-2.text: Press your thumb and first finger together. Breathe in slowly through your nose.

qs-r2-3.text: And breathe out through your mouth, long and slow, like you are fogging a window.

qs-r2-5.text: And a long, slow breath out. Let your shoulders drop.

qs-r2-8.text: This urge is a wave. It has already started to peak, and it will pass whether you smoke or not. You do not have to fight it. Just let it roll through.

qs-r2-9.text: Now squeeze both fists tight. Hold the squeeze. Feel the strength in your hands.

qs-r5-1.text: You are having a craving, and you came here first. Good. For the next five minutes, we are going to ride this wave together. You can keep your eyes open.

qs-r5-10.text: Keep breathing, slow and easy. Breathe in, making room. And breathe out, softening.

qs-r5-11.text: An urge is like a wave in the ocean. It builds, it reaches a peak, and then it falls away. It always falls away. You are not the wave. You are the one watching it.

qs-r5-12.text: If it helps, press your palms together firmly in front of your chest. Push, and hold. Feel how strong you are.

qs-r5-13.text: And let go. Shake out your hands.

qs-r5-14.text: Check in with the urge again. Give it a new number. It may have dropped, or changed shape. Even if it is the same, you have just proven that you can feel it without obeying it.

qs-r5-15.text: Take one more slow breath in. Think of one reason you are quitting. Just one. Hold it in your mind.

qs-r5-16.text: And breathe out. That reason is still true, and you are still free.

qs-r5-17.text: The wave has moved through. Now change what you are doing: drink a glass of water, step outside, or message someone. You handled this. Take that with you.

qs-r5-2.text: Start with a slow breath in through your nose.

qs-r5-3.text: And breathe out slowly, through your mouth.

qs-r5-5.text: And slowly out. Let your jaw and your shoulders loosen.

qs-r5-6.text: Now, get curious. Where in your body do you feel this urge? It might be in your chest, your throat, your hands, or your stomach. Just find it.

qs-r5-7.text: Notice what it actually feels like. Is it tight? Restless? Warm? Empty? You do not need to change it. Just describe it to yourself, the way a scientist would.

qs-r5-8.text: In your mind, give it a number from zero to ten. However strong it is right now is okay.

qs-r5-9.text: Now breathe around that feeling. As you breathe in, give it space. As you breathe out, let the edges of it soften.

shs-b-1.text: You can let your eyes close. Let each breath flow in and out without any effort. I will be quiet now, and let you breathe with the wind.

shs-b-2.text: You are doing well. If your mind has wandered, simply come back to the sound of the wind. Soft belly. Soft shoulders. Soft face.

shs-deep-1.text: Your body is growing heavy now. Your legs are heavy, and warm, sinking down into the bed. Your arms are heavy. Your whole body, resting.

shs-deep-2.text: Imagine a single leaf, high in the trees, letting go of its branch. Drifting down, slowly, turning in the soft air. Down, and down.

shs-deep-3.text: With every breath out, you drift a little deeper, like that leaf. Down through the quiet forest. Deeper, and deeper.

shs-deep-4.text: Ten. Drifting down. Nine. Eight. Deeper still. Seven. Six. Five. Softer and heavier. Four. Three. Two. One. Resting on the soft forest floor, deeply at rest.

shs-fade-1.text: Drifting deeper now. Warm, and heavy, and safe.

shs-fade-3.text: Nothing to do. Nowhere to be.

shs-heart-1.text: As you keep breathing, let your attention rest in the center of your chest. Imagine each breath flowing in and out, gently, around your heart.

shs-heart-2.text: And now, if you like, think of someone you care for. Or a place where you feel safe. There is nothing to do. Just let a little warmth be here, as you breathe.

shs-heart-3.text: Let that warmth spread. Through your chest. Into your shoulders. All the way down your arms, and into your hands.

shs-pre-1.text: Welcome. This is a breathing practice to steady your heart, and then to carry you gently into sleep. Lie down, and let your body be comfortable. Let your arms rest beside you.

shs-pre-2.text: In a moment you will hear the wind moving through the trees. As the wind rises, breathe in through your nose. As it settles, breathe out, slowly. The breath out is a little longer than the breath in.

shs-pre-3.text: These are gentle breaths, not big ones. If you ever feel light headed, simply breathe normally, and let the wind carry on without you.

shs-rel-1.text: Now you can let the breathing go. Let the wind drift on without you, and let your breath find its own slow, sleepy rhythm.

shs-sug-1.text: Here, in this stillness, sleep comes easily. You do not need to do anything. Sleep comes to you, the way night comes to the forest.

shs-sug-2.text: Tonight, you sleep deeply. Your sleep is deep, and steady, and restoring. Deeper, and deeper, all through the night.

shs-sug-3.text: Your heart is calm. Your breath is slow. Your body knows how to rest, and it rests deeply now.

shs-sug-4.text: If you stir in the night, you simply turn over, and drift straight back down. Deeper each time. Like a leaf settling, softly, to the ground.

shs-sug-5.text: Any sounds around you only carry you deeper. Every breath out takes you deeper into slow, peaceful sleep.

shs-warm-1.text: Let us begin. In, as the wind rises. And out, as it settles.

shs-warm-2.text: Good. Now the wind slows a little more. Smooth, and easy.

sl-deep-1.text: Now imagine that you are floating on calm, warm water, in the quiet of the evening. The water holds you completely. You are perfectly safe.

sl-deep-2.text: And slowly, comfortably, you begin to sink beneath the surface, where everything is quiet and still. You can breathe easily here. With every breath, you drift a little deeper.

sl-deep-3.text: Deeper, and deeper. The sounds of the day fade far above you. Down here, there is only soft, blue stillness.

sl-deep-4.text: I will count slowly from ten down to one. With each number, you sink deeper into rest. Ten. Sinking down. Nine. Deeper and deeper. Eight. So heavy, and so calm.

sl-deep-5.text: Seven. Drifting down. Six. Deeper still. Five. Thoughts are slowing, and floating away.

sl-deep-6.text: Four. Deeper and deeper. Three. So quiet now. Two. Almost at the bottom. And one. Resting in the deepest, softest place.

sl-fade-1.text: Sinking deeper now. Heavy, and warm, and safe.

sl-fade-3.text: Nothing to do. Nowhere to be.

sl-ind-1.text: Take a slow, comfortable breath in. And let it go, with a long, soft sigh.

sl-ind-2.text: Once more, breathe in gently. And breathe out, letting the mattress take all of your weight.

sl-ind-3.text: Now let your breathing settle into its own slow rhythm. With every breath out, your body grows a little heavier, and a little warmer.

sl-ind-4.text: Feel your forehead become smooth. Your eyelids are heavy and still. Your jaw loosens, and your tongue rests softly in your mouth.

sl-ind-5.text: Your shoulders sink into the bed. Your arms grow heavy, all the way down to your hands. Your fingers are loose and still.

sl-ind-6.text: Your back lets go, one small muscle at a time. Your chest and your stomach rise and fall, slowly, without any effort at all.

sl-ind-7.text: Your hips are heavy. Your legs are heavy. That warm heaviness flows down through your knees, your ankles, to the very tips of your toes. Your whole body is sinking into rest.

sl-pre-1.text: It is time to rest now. Settle into your bed, and let your body find the position it likes best. There is nothing more to do today. You can simply listen, or let my voice drift into the background.

sl-pre-2.text: If you fall asleep before I finish, that is exactly right. You do not need to follow every word.

sl-sug-1.text: Here, in this deep stillness, sleep comes to you easily. You do not have to make it happen. Sleep finds you, the way evening finds the sky.

sl-sug-2.text: Tonight, you sleep deeply. Your sleep is deep, and steady, and restoring. Deeper and deeper, all through the night.

sl-sug-3.text: As you sleep deeply, your body repairs itself. Your mind gently sorts through the day, and sets it down. Everything that needs your attention can wait until morning.

sl-sug-4.text: If you stir in the night, you simply turn over, and sink straight back down. Deeper each time. Sleep welcomes you back.

sl-sug-5.text: Any sounds around you only carry you deeper. Every breath out takes you deeper. Deeper and deeper into slow, peaceful sleep.

sl-sug-6.text: And when morning comes, at the right time for you, you wake feeling rested and clear. But that is a long way off. For now, there is only rest.
